questions.question: Who is responsible for monetary policy in South Africa?
options: The Minister of Finance
The South African Reserve Bank
Parliament
The commercial banks jointly

questions.question: The SARB's inflation target band is:
options: 2% exactly

questions.question: Which quick test identifies whether an instrument is monetary or fiscal?
options: Ask how large the amount involved is
Ask whether it affects households or firms
Ask whose hand is on it — the Reserve Bank (monetary) or the government's budget (fiscal)
Ask whether it is announced on television

questions.question: A policy that deliberately slows down spending in the economy is called:
options: Contractionary
Expansionary
Distributive
Neutral

subtopics.title: The SARB's Move — the Repo Rate

questions.question: The repo rate is the interest rate at which:
options: Commercial banks lend to their customers
The SARB lends money to commercial banks
The government borrows from foreign lenders
Households borrow for home loans

questions.question: With inflation above the target band, the SARB is most likely to:
options: Lower the repo rate
Increase government spending
Raise the repo rate
Reduce VAT

questions.question: Which chain correctly orders the transmission of a repo rate increase?
options: Repo up → prime up → loans dearer → spending slows → price pressure eases
Repo up → taxes up → spending up → inflation up
Repo up → prime down → borrowing rises → inflation falls
Repo up → government spending falls → exports rise → inflation falls

questions.question: What honest trade-off comes with raising the repo rate to fight inflation?
options: It weakens the SARB's independence
It automatically raises government debt
There is no trade-off
It cools growth and can cost jobs in the short run

subtopics.title: The Minister's Toolbox — Two Fiscal Instruments

questions.question: The two main instruments of fiscal policy are:
options: The repo rate and the prime rate
Government spending and taxation
Exports and imports
Savings and investment

questions.question: To fight inflation using fiscal policy, the government would:
options: Increase spending and cut taxes
Lower the repo rate
Print more money
Reduce spending growth and/or raise taxes

questions.question: 'The Minister of Finance raises the repo rate to fight inflation.' What is wrong with this statement?
options: The repo rate is controlled by the SARB, not the minister
The repo rate cannot fight inflation
Inflation is fought only with taxes
Nothing — the statement is correct

questions.question: In a recession, expansionary fiscal policy would involve:
options: Higher taxes and lower spending
Raising the repo rate
Increased government spending and/or tax cuts
Reducing social grants

subtopics.title: Comparing the Two Policies — and Answering Like an Economist

questions.question: Which comparison of the two policies is accurate?
options: Monetary policy is fast but blunt; fiscal policy is slower but can be targeted
Fiscal policy is decided every two months; monetary policy once a year
Both are decided by the SARB
Monetary policy only affects the government

questions.question: Who feels a repo rate increase first?
options: Exporters
People with no debt
Borrowers — households with home loans and indebted firms
Foreign tourists

questions.question: What happens if the SARB tightens while the government spends freely?
options: Inflation falls twice as fast
The repo rate stops working entirely
The budget automatically balances
The policies work against each other, and the SARB may need to tighten even harder

subtopics.title: Two Drivers, Two Different Steering Wheels

questions.question: Using the 'whose hand is on it?' test, a rise in VAT is:
options: Monetary policy, because it affects prices
Fiscal policy — VAT belongs to the Budget, and the Budget is the Minister's
Neither, because VAT is collected by shops
Monetary policy, because the SARB approves it

questions.question: In the balloon picture, which move lets air OUT of the economy?
options: Cutting income tax
Increasing social grants
Raising taxes and cutting government spending
Lowering the repo rate

questions.question: Why does it matter that the Reserve Bank is independent?
options: It can make an unpopular decision without waiting for political approval
It means the Bank pays no taxes
It means the Bank sets the Budget
It allows the Bank to print unlimited money

questions.question: The Reserve Bank's job, put simply, is to look after:
options: The government's spending plans
The profits of the commercial banks
The number of people employed by the state
What your money is worth — keeping inflation inside the 3% to 6% band

subtopics.title: How One Number in Pretoria Reaches Your Street

questions.question: The repo rate is the rate charged when:
options: You borrow from your bank for a car
A shop offers a store card
The Reserve Bank lends to the commercial banks
The government borrows abroad

questions.question: Told as a story, which order is correct?
options: Repo up, prime up, loans dearer, spending pulls in, price rises slow down
Repo up, taxes up, spending up, inflation up
Repo up, prime down, borrowing rises, inflation falls
Repo up, grants up, spending falls, prices fall

questions.question: Why does a family's bond repayment rise after a repo increase?
options: The government adds a levy to home loans
The bank's own borrowing costs more, so it raises the prime lending rate it charges customers
House prices rise automatically
The SARB collects the extra directly

questions.question: What is the honest cost of using the repo rate to cool inflation?
options: There is no cost — it only affects banks
It weakens the rand permanently
It automatically raises taxes
Growth slows and some jobs are lost in the short run, and borrowers feel it before anyone else

subtopics.title: The Budget's Two Taps — Fast Tool, Slow Tool

questions.question: The Minister of Finance's two taps are:
options: The repo rate and the prime rate
Government spending and taxation
Imports and exports
Wages and profits

questions.question: 'The Minister of Finance raises the repo rate to fight inflation.' What is wrong?
options: Nothing — the statement is correct
Inflation cannot be fought with interest rates
The wrong hand is on the lever: the repo rate belongs to the Reserve Bank
Only VAT can fight inflation

questions.question: Which sentence captures the fast-versus-aimed comparison?
options: Both tools are equally fast and equally aimed
Fiscal policy is fast and blunt; monetary policy is slow and aimed
Only fiscal policy can fight inflation
Monetary policy is fast but blunt — it hits every borrower; fiscal policy is slower but can be aimed at a tax, a programme or a province

questions.question: If the Reserve Bank tightens while government keeps spending freely:
options: The two work against each other, and the Bank usually has to tighten harder
Inflation falls twice as fast
The repo rate stops working
The Budget balances automatically
